Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Snap shares sank over 10% when the Snapchat parent missed on revenue and daily active users in its third-quarter earnings report Wednesday. Here's how the company did compared with analysts' expectations: Earnings per share : $0.19 adj. vs. $0.16 expected, according to LSEG Revenue : $1.72 billion vs. $1.73 billion expected, according to LSEG Global daily active users : 495 million vs. 499 million expected, according to StreetAccount Global average revenue per user, or ARPU : $3.48 vs. $3.48 expected, according to StreetAccount Sales in Snap's third quarter jumped 14% year-over-year while net income came in at $56 million, compared to the $104 million net loss it logged the prior year. Snap's third-quarter adjusted earnings came in at $383 million, topping the $337 million that analysts were projecting, according to StreetAccount. The Snapchat parent said fourth-quarter revenue should come in between $1.95 billion and $1.99 billion. The midpoint of that figure is higher than Wall Street's estimates of $1.95 billion. Fourth-quarter adjusted earnings are expected to come in between $490 million and $525 million. Analysts were expecting that figure to be $498 million. Snap executives said in an investor letter that the company plans for globally monthly active users to become its "primary audience metric" starting in its first quarter for 2027. The company also said it has 977 MAU for the quarter. "Daily engagement has historically been stable as a percentage of monthly engagement, but we do not intend to optimize Snapchat around daily use at the expense of long-term value for our community," the investor letter said. "A longer-term horizon better aligns our reported metrics with the product and safety decisions that strengthen relationships, create lasting utility, and support broader, more durable audience growth." Snap chief commercial officer Ronan Harris told analysts during an earnings call that lower spending by unspecified consumer packaged goods, or CPG, companies impacted third-quarter sales. Harris attributed the curbed CPG spending to "macro pressures in the U.S. and also the Middle East." "As we look ahead, we're seeing very positive signs of growth from diversified verticals like financial services in the U.S.," Harris said. The United Arab Emirates pledged to strengthen its energy infrastructure, saying the Middle East war demonstrated the value of investing in alternative supply routes and spare capacity to ride out times of crisis. Photographer: Walaa Alshaer/Bloomberg via Getty Images Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images Rising energy demand is creating new investment opportunities even as geopolitical risks and uncertain oil prices challenge the industry. Baker Hughes CEO Lorenzo Simonelli is optimistic about the longer-term outlook, pointing to AI, population growth and developing nations as factors supporting continued energy demand growth. "I think we have a 'demand decade' ahead of us," Simonelli told CNBC's Dan Murphy on " Access Middle East " at the ADIPEC energy conference in Abu Dhabi. "We're looking at very much seeing capital investments improve and increase over time," as growing consumption will require additional infrastructure to support demand. watch now VIDEO 7:11 07:11 Energy system has to be more resilient: Baker Hughes CEO Access Middle East However, turning that demand into profitability may be a challenge. Markus Krebber, CEO of German energy company RWE, said AI and electrification were driving electricity demand, but geopolitical tensions, supply chain pressures and higher interest rates were complicating investment decisions. "You have huge investment opportunity, but on the other hand, a very challenging investment environment," Krebber said during a separate ADIPEC discussion. On planned expansions in computing capacity and the power needed to support them, he said "it's going to come, but it probably comes slow." The wide range of global energy demand forecasts is an important consideration in investment decisions, given that new oil and gas projects can take years to develop and remain in production for decades, BP CEO Meg O'Neill said at ADIPEC. She also highlighted the uncertainty surrounding oil prices, saying that "we need to plan our business for a lower-price environment." Industry activity Industry activity is expected to rise by a low-single-digit percentage in 2027, according to Simonelli. The Middle East conflict has highlighted the need for more resilient energy infrastructure, including additional storage and pipelines, he said. "If you look at the energy system, though, what it really means is it's going to have to be more resilient," Simonelli said. "That means more storage. It means more pipelines. It means eliminating choke points that exist today." Schneider Electric CEO Olivier Blum noted that some projects in the Persian Gulf have slowed because of the Middle East conflict. However, "in the mid-term, I would say the opportunity for more infrastructure has even increased," he told CNBC. watch now VIDEO 2:25 02:25 Sharp unwind for oil if no Iran military escalation after midterms Access Middle East The investment equation also depends on the supply outlook, of course. Oil markets could face oversupply in 2027 and 2028, Richard Bronze, co-founder and head of geopolitics at energy consultancy Energy Aspects, told CNBC in a separate interview. Supply-demand forecasts, including those from Energy Aspects, "project an oversupplied market 2027, 2028 — if we get Middle Eastern flows back to normal," Bronze said. headlines.summary: Figma is letting clients use more artificial intelligence features for the same price. The company would like the move to boost results in the long term.
headlines.article_text: Figma (FIG) Q3 earnings report 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Figma exceeded consensus on third-quarter results and guidance. Net loss narrowed to $81.3 million from a loss of $1.10 billion a year ago. The company sees revenue growth slowing, but it's trading off short-term revenue for long-term benefits, finance chief Praveer Melwani said. In this article FIG Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Figma signage appears at the New York Stock Exchange in New York as the company prepares for its shares to begin trading on July 31, 2025. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Figma shares tumbled 7% in extended trading after the company reported third-quarter results and guidance that surpassed Wall Street's predictions. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: Earnings per share: 10 cents adjusted vs. 5 cents expected Revenue: $391.4 million vs. $375.8 million expected Figma's revenue grew about 43% year over year in the quarter, according to a statement . Net loss narrowed to $81.3 million, or 15 cents per share, compared with a loss of $1.10 billion, or $2.72 per share, a year earlier. The company's 12% adjusted operating margin exceeded the 6.1% consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount. Executives lifted the full-year forecast. Figma now anticipates an 11% operating margin, up from 9% as of August, and $1.497 billion to $1.499 billion in revenue, compared with $1.463 billion to $1.467 billion before. Analysts surveyed by LSEG were looking for $1.471 billion in 2026 revenue. The company sees fourth-quarter revenue growth slowing to about 33%. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted 28% growth. Figma's announcement comes a day after highly valued design software startup Canva said it would cut 22% of its employees. Read more CNBC tech news Elon Musk's record election bet backfired. The backlash may reach beyond one billionaire Apple warns of risks related to AI agents behaving in 'unintended or unpredictable' ways AMD's data center revenue nearly doubles and Lisa Su expects growth to accelerate Google responds to political backlash over removing search from schools that ban AI Shares have come down about 41% so far in 2026, while the S&P 500 index has gained 12%. Earlier this year, investors became concerned that artificial intelligence models could pose a competitive risk to Figma. Across much of software, AI panic has largely subsided as incumbents have posted persistent growth. Figma wants to benefit from the rising adoption of AI to build websites and apps. During the quarter, the company started giving more AI credits to clients while maintaining prices. "What that means is you're potentially trading off near-term revenue, investing in your customers, and then allowing yourself to then grow durably over the long term," Figma's finance chief, Praveer Melwani, told CNBC in an interview on Wednesday. The number of weekly users working at organizations that spend over $10,000 on Figma who used AI credits increased by almost 50% during the quarter, Figma said in the statement. The share of work the company's own AI model performs doubled, and the rate of people undoing AI-generated work has fallen . "If there's certain actions that we can power for our customers at lower latency, lower cost, or similar quality to third party, we're open to that as well," Melwani said. Figma is increasing its focus on cybersecurity, said Dylan Field, Figma's co-founder and CEO. In recent months, AI agents have infiltrated systems at Hugging Face and other companies. Clients aren't asking Figma to become a security vendor, but the company must scrutinize "the security of all of our vendors right now," Field said.
